findings.text: Variant C shows the brand word "Section" but builds its nav from Core's children and points the logo at Framework, even though Section's parent is Core (core/Sidebar/variants/c/page.js:655 and :674). That contradicts the idea it is meant to show ("the word becomes the current page, the sidebar shows that page's own nav"). Give it `root: Section` and send the logo to Core.

Walkthrough step 1, "The section element", has its "Open it live" link going to /framework/core/Sidebar/variants/ when it should go to /framework/ui/section/ (core/Sidebar/variants/walkthrough/page.js:1073 in the diff).

"Who owns the rail?" has no H1: render() is overridden and the page opens on a plain paragraph (rail/page.js:933; see the rail sheet.png). Every other variant keeps a heading, and a reader landing here has no title.

On pages A–D the H1 comes after the back link, an intro paragraph and a blockquote, so at 1280 and 1920 it sits a third of the way down the screen (Sidebar-variants-c/sheet.png, -d/sheet.png). The owner said "don't compete with the H1", and the demo ends up hiding it instead. Put the H1 first and the quote under it.

The floating page does not match the owner's 12:05 AM spec. The spec asks for a nav that stays in place at full height with the same padding-top, and a white page that scrolls on its own. What was built is a sticky nav at `top: 0`, so it butts against the viewport once you scroll, inside a page that scrolls with the document. The white page also hugs its content, so a short tab leaves a gray void below it at 3440 (floating.js:297–304 and :329; Page-layout-floating/sheet.png). The task log admits the last point as a caveat, but it is a gap, not an option.

`.floating-well:not(.ui-section)` (floating.js:286) exists only because the floating page's Overview reuses the real class names inside section(), which pulls in the real styles. Simpler: label the diagram with its own demo classes, or give section() an explicit label argument, and delete the special case and its 20-line comment.
floating.js:263–264 sets `padding: var(--pad)` and then `padding-top: var(--pad)` again. The second line does nothing.

ui/section: at every width the borders are barely visible, and the "bleed" demo does not look full-width. It sits in the same narrow column as the rest (ui-section/sheet.png, 73–89% empty). Nothing in the static shot shows the hover label, so the section-hover walkthrough image carries the whole message. Check that `.bleed` really bleeds inside `content()`.

The deliverable asks for 1280 and 3440 for each variant, but only B was shot at both widths (walkthrough STEPS). At 3440 every variant page is an ~590px column in an 85%-empty screen (Sidebar-variants-d/sheet.png), and the rail page's two stages spread 1400px apart with small rails (rail/sheet.png).

Counts disagree. The variants index description says "Five pages", walkthrough step 2 says "Four ways", and the walkthrough description says "six sidebar variants". The walkthrough also covers the section element and the floating page but lives under core/Sidebar/variants/walkthrough/, so a reader looking for section won't find it there.
The rail page's brand_header() is a copy of variant A's header() (rail/page.js:857). Importing A's header, with the root as a parameter, would avoid the duplicate.
The requirements ask for "a Decision on the card", and I could not verify it from these files. The walkthrough's last step only says the decision "lives on the task's card".
Scope: the floating-page move came from the owner's later words, not from requirements.md. It is fine to include, but the requirements should name it so the next reviewer knows it was asked for.
